name: Divine Nature & Trinity
description: Scholastic and doctrinal questions on God's being, eternity, immutability, infinity, perfection, oneness, and goodness, and on the Trinity, the divine persons, processions, the Word, and the Holy Spirit.

name: Divine Knowledge & Providence
description: How God knows himself, singulars, future contingents, and evils, together with providence, predestination, foreknowledge versus fate, and the divine ordering of good and evil powers.

name: Angels & Demons
description: The nature, knowledge, movement, number, creation, and beatitude of angels, and the obstinacy, blindness, and punishment of demons.

name: Creation & Metaphysics
description: Creation ex nihilo, prime matter, the eternity of the world, and abstract questions on being, the one, the convertibility of good and being, and the nature and cause of evil.

name: Soul, Intellect & Will
description: The powers of the soul, appetite, the irascible and concupiscible, free will, grace and original sin, and how the human intellect knows singulars, itself, and the will.

name: Christ & Incarnation
description: Why God became man and suffered, who suffered on the cross, Christ as universal savior and Prince of Peace, the temptation of Christ, the cross, and the penitent thief.

name: Last Things & Resurrection
description: Resurrection of the body, final judgment separating just from impious, the saved seeing God, the punishments of the wicked, Antichrist, and the end of the age.

name: Sin, Penance & Mercy
description: Forgiveness through contrition, the role of the priest, temporal versus eternal punishment, mercy toward the impious, repentance, and reconciliation with enemies.

name: Prayer, Devotion & the Soul
description: Dialogues of the soul seeking God, how to invoke and find him, conversion, the bride seeking her beloved, and the efficacy of the just man's prayer.

name: Scripture & Exegesis
description: Question-answer exchanges interpreting biblical texts and their figurative meaning, and the modes of sacred discourse such as history, prophecy, proverb, and type.

name: Saints, Miracles & Martyrdom
description: Hagiographic exchanges on raised corpses, apostles and bishop-saints, desert fathers, endurance under torture for Christ's name, and Christian narrative of God's saving wonders.

name: Marriage, Virginity & Celibacy
description: Patristic and humanist debate on the goods of matrimony versus virginity, why Christ abstained, sterile unions, betrothals, dowries, and the matching of spouses.

name: Pagan Gods & Mythology
description: Apologetic interrogation and explanation of Greek and Roman deities and mythic figures (Jupiter, Saturn, Bacchus, Orpheus) as euhemerized men, allegorized elements, or what their fables signify.

name: Pagan Worship, Omens & Sacrifice
description: Debates over sacrifices, divine images, oracles and haruspices, the cult of many gods versus the true God, sacrificial portents, and the origin of religious error.

name: Canon Law
description: Decretal questions on ecclesiastical procedure, delegated judges, appeals, ordination and defects barring orders, benefices, tithes, and church property.

name: Roman & Civil Law
description: Classical-law questions on legacies, actions in rem and in personam, stipulations, theft, and Isidoran definitions of ius naturale, civile, gentium, and lex.

name: Justice, Crime & Punishment
description: Legal accusation and innocence, statutes, just deserts, crimes and their penalties, who deserves blame, and the legitimacy of killing or sparing.

name: Rhetoric, Oratory & Poetics
description: Handbook theory of rhetoric and the orator, parts of a case, exordia and witnesses, the craft and ranking of poetry, and judgments on style and bombast.

name: Forensic & Political Oratory
description: Courtroom and assembly attack speech, accusation versus innocence, denunciation of Catiline, suborned testimony, and senatorial deliberation over public policy and conspirators.

name: Grammar & Parts of Speech
description: Schoolroom catechism defining and classifying the partes orationis and their accidents, declensions, conjugations, cases, and forms.

name: Etymology, Definition & Wordplay
description: Word-origin and definitional exchanges (why a term, spelling, or vowel quantity is used), proper Latin diction, and trick answers, puns, or Greek-versus-Latin riddles.

name: Cosmology & Natural Science
description: Natural-philosophical questions on the heavens, the moon's light, the sun's course and zodiac, the sphere, and physical phenomena such as lightning, thunder, winds, comets, and fire.

name: Arts, Crafts & Expertise
description: Exchanges on the liberal disciplines and trades, assigning tasks to the proper specialist (doctor, helmsman, farmer, smith), and the desire to become wise in one's art.

name: Health, Body & Medicine
description: Pairs on illness, pain, wounds, cures and remedies, the body's afflictions, food and diet, gluttony, and the management of one's physical condition.

name: War, Conquest & Empire
description: Campaigns, battles, generals against Hannibal or Attila, captured towns and conquered peoples, soldiers' arms and feats, crusade, and Rome as lord of nations.

name: Tyranny, Kingship & Political Rule
description: Rulership and its abuse, who should reign, choosing the worthiest heir, the fears and prerogatives of kings, and just rule versus cruelty and mere will.

name: Court Intrigue & Royal Conflict
description: Dramatic and historical dialogue plotting assassination and usurpation, naming poisoners and accomplices, Merovingian feuds, broken pacts, and dynastic vengeance.

name: Crime, Atrocity & Bloodshed
description: Pairs narrating or probing violent deeds: poisonings, murder of kin, slaughtered children, and the gruesome carnage of tragedy.

name: Magic & the Supernatural
description: Witches, Thessalian sorceresses, animated statues, reanimated corpses, spells and transformations, and guarding the dead against the versipelles.

name: Adventure & Romance Narrative
description: Picaresque and Gesta-Romanorum story dialogue of bandits, shipwrecks, captivity, kings' daughters as brides, pledges, proscriptions, and recognitions between travelers.

name: Identity, Lineage & Recognition
description: Exchanges establishing who someone is, their name, homeland, parentage, age, descent, or staging the reunion of long-lost kin (De qua progenie es tu?).

name: Love, Desire & Wit
description: Erotic and amorous exchanges on Venus, Cupid and Psyche, courtesans and mistresses, the power of Amor, measuring affection, and bantering elegiac retorts.

name: Friendship & Social Conduct
description: Dialogue on the definition, testing, and fidelity of true amicitia, greetings, hospitality, drinking companions, patronage, and faithfulness between companions.

name: Death, Grief & Consolation
description: Reflective and dramatic exchanges on the brevity of life, the inescapability of death, suicide, summoning shades across the Styx, mourning, and consoling the bereaved.

name: Virtue, Wisdom & the Good Life
description: Ethical questions defining the highest good, the vir bonus, the blessed life, the invulnerable sage, self-knowledge, and the difference between being called and being good.

name: Money, Wealth & Avarice
description: Exchanges on prices, debts, commerce, true riches versus need, contentment with little, and avarice as going beyond enough or as poverty itself.

name: Passions, Anger & Self-Mastery
description: Largely Stoic exchanges on whether the wise man should be angry, the management of wrath and vengeance, conquering vice, and raising the spirit above fortune.

name: Fate, Fortune & Providence
description: Pairs on whether fate or chance governs life, why misfortune befalls good men, the divine ordering of events, and the proper stance toward Fortune.

name: Slavery, Servitude & Freedom
description: Questions turning on enslaved or freed status, manumission, ransom, and the legal threshold between bondage and liberty.

name: Domestic & Everyday Affairs
description: Mundane household and daily-life talk: greetings, whereabouts, errands, meals, dinner invitations, lodging, and small talk, plus mockery, jests, and barbed retorts.
